title: Former Tesla engineer says AI will create more 'fake jobs' — not mass unemployment
excerpt: Tejas Bhakta, the founder of Morph and a former Tesla machine learning engineer, said a lot of today's jobs are basically "UBI right now."
content_html:
By Ben Shimkus

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-25T17:48:54.606Z

Worried that AI could replace your job? Tejas Bhakta says he thinks the tech will do the opposite — and add to our pile of useless work.

"Some people have this take that we're going to have mass unemployment as a result of this," he said during an interview with MTS Live. "I almost feel the opposite. Like, I think we're going to have more bullshit jobs. Just way more."

Bhakta, a former Tesla machine-learning engineer, is now the founder of Morph, an AI-infrastructure startup that was in Y Combinator's Summer 2023 batch.

"Basically most jobs are UBI right now." Morph founder @tejasybhakta argues that AI could create even more bullshit jobs rather than lead to mass unemployment: "Most people are in jobs that don't need to exist. These procurement officers that are putting out this paperwork that doesn't need to be done to sign this doc that no one cares about or will ever read. "Basically most jobs are UBI right now. That's sort of the hottest take in there." "Some people have this take that we're gonna have more mass unemployment as a result of this. I almost feel the opposite. I think we're gonna have more bullshit jobs, just way more." "Pre-AGI, 40% of jobs were just not really actually doing anything. In order for that organism to keep surviving, it needs these people to have UBI, otherwise the economy falls apart." "So we'll just have more jobs that are fake jobs while AGI does all the work." @morphllm

— MTS (@MTSlive) November 24, 2026

Bhakta's take is different from the roller-coaster warnings coming from other Silicon Valley-based executives. In May 2025, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei cautioned that AI could wipe out 50% of all entry-level white-collar jobs. AI's top bosses have adjusted their tone in 2026, saying the technology could create a new hiring boom cycle.

Bhakta is closer to that boom cycle camp — but with a less rosy tint.

His view: Our current economy is filled with "jobs that don't need to exist," including procurement workers generating paperwork "that no one cares about or will ever read."

"Basically most jobs are UBI right now," he said, referring to universal basic income. He estimated that 40% of internet jobs are "not actually doing anything."

He told Business Insider that his view has been shaped by his time working in Big Tech companies. He said it was common to see teams work on projects that never shipped.

"I don't even know if it's an inefficiency," he said. "I think it's just a necessary thing."

He added that he isn't arguing that people should be fired.

On MTS Live, Bhakta predicted that AI will add to that paperwork morass — but those jobs will continue to serve as an unofficial safety net.

"It's almost like the organism of the US, like, in order for that organism to keep surviving, it needs these people to have UBI," he said. "Otherwise, the economy falls apart. And so, we'll just have more jobs that are fake jobs while AGI does all of the work."
